title: Sumihiro invariant affine neighbourhoods on normal torus schemes
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $r\geq0$ be an integer, and let $T=(\mathbf G_{m,F})^r$ be the split torus [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-gm-ga], with the trivial group for $r=0$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which is normal: every local ring is an integral domain integrally closed in its field of fractions [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose a morphism $a:T\times_F X\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is an action, meaning that $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(t,a(u,x))=a(tu,x)$ as identities of morphisms. For every point $x\in |X|$ there exists an affine open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] containing $x$ such that $a|_{T\times_F U}$ factors through $U$. The resulting action on $U$ makes its inclusion equivariant. Neither smoothness, projectivity, integrality of $X$, faithfulness of the action nor a characteristic restriction is assumed.

source.place: Supporting input to the concentration prerequisite of Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480; not asserted to occur in Milne. WANTED: H. Sumihiro, Equivariant completion, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 14 (1974), 1--28, Corollary 2, invariant affine neighbourhood theorem for normal torus varieties. Here stated for normal separated finite-type schemes, allowing finitely many disjoint normal components and ineffective actions. No Stacks tag is asserted for this theorem; the paper is absent locally.

proof.text: If $X$ is empty there is no point to treat. Otherwise fix $x\in |X|$. In Laurent coordinates $T=\operatorname{Spec}F[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ is affine of finite type. Apply [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] to the lattice $\mathbf Z^r$: $T$ is smooth and its coordinate ring is an integral domain. Its spectrum is nonempty and irreducible (the zero prime has dense closure), hence connected. Thus the group hypotheses of [lem-sfb-sumihiro-invariant-quasiprojective-open] hold. That node supplies a normal separated finite-type invariant quasi-projective open $W\subseteq X$ with $x\in W$. This step uses normality exactly as assumed, not smoothness of $X$; $r=0$ gives $T=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and still meets the group hypotheses.

source.place: Section 13f, Definition 13.45, supporting Sumihiro neighborhood input (WANTED, as specified in its node); Definition 12.14 for split tori. Agent assembly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-quasiprojective-equivariant-immersion] to $W$ and $G=T$ to obtain a finite-dimensional rational representation $V\ne0$ and an equivariant immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(V)=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$. Normality implies reducedness since an integral domain has no nonzero nilpotents. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-invariant-boundary-ideals] to the reduced locally closed image of $j$. Obtain the invariant reduced projective closure $Z$ and its invariant reduced boundary $B$, with $W=Z\setminus |B|$ as open schemes. In particular $p=j(x)$ lies in $Z$ and outside $B$. The same node makes every boundary degree piece $I(B)_d$ a finite-dimensional rational $T$-representation. Smoothness of $T$, required for this scheme-level closure statement, was checked in step 1.

source.place: Section 7e (linear actions), and supporting equivariant immersion and invariant boundary-ideal statements; Sumihiro input is WANTED. Agent assembly.

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal], the homogeneous ideal $I= igoplus_d I(B)_d$ realizes $B$ as $\operatorname{Proj}(S/I)$. In the prime-ideal description [def-pc-proj], $p
otin B$ means $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p_p$. Choose a homogeneous $f\in I_d\setminus\mathfrak p_p$: if all homogeneous components were in the prime, every element of $I$ would be in it. We can arrange $d>0$. Indeed if $d=0$, choose a coordinate $z_i
otin\mathfrak p_p$ (the prime does not contain the irrelevant ideal); then $fz_i\in I_1\setminus\mathfrak p_p$ by primality. This includes $B=\varnothing$, when the ideal can contain constants. No closed-point or rational-point assumption on $x$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space; homogeneous prime definition in Proj.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to the representation $I(B)_d$ from step 2. Write $f=\sum_\chi f_\chi$ in its finitely many weight spaces. At least one $f_\chi$ is outside $\mathfrak p_p$, since otherwise their sum lies in the prime. Fix such a polynomial $h=f_\chi$. It is homogeneous of the same positive degree $d$, vanishes on $B$, and satisfies $g\cdot h=\chi(g)h$ after every commutative algebra extension. This uses the representation on the boundary ideal itself; decomposing in the ambient $S_d$ without proving preservation of the ideal would not justify vanishing of its weight components.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234--235, applied to the boundary degree subrepresentation; supporting boundary statement in step 2.

proof.text: Set $U=j^{-1}D_+(h)$. It contains $x$ because $h\notin\mathfrak p_p$. Since $h$ vanishes on $B$, $D_+(h)\cap |B|=\varnothing$; the identification $W=Z\setminus |B|$ from step 2 therefore identifies $U$ as a scheme with $Z\cap D_+(h)$. The positive-degree chart $D_+(h)$ is affine by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. Its intersection with the closed subscheme $Z$ is affine by the affine quotient-ring characterization [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $U$ is an affine open of $W$ and of $X$. It is essential here that the polynomial vanishes on the whole boundary: an arbitrary affine projective chart would give only a locally closed subscheme.

source.place: Tag 01M4, lemma-standard-open, and the Proj affine chart construction; closed immersions on affines: Schemes Tag 01IQ, definition-closed-immersion.

proof.text: For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $g\in T(A)$ and local generator $v$ of a line representing a point of $\mathbf P(V)(A)$, the contragredient polynomial convention and the eigenvector identity give $h(\rho(g)v)=\chi(g)^{-1}h(v)$. The factor $\chi(g)$ is a unit. Hence the nonvanishing open $D_+(h)$ is invariant, including on nonreduced test algebras; checking in local generators suffices because they differ by units and $h$ is homogeneous. Equivariance of $j$ then maps the universal point of $T\times_F U$ into $U$. By [def-weil-open-immersion] this gives a unique factorization of $a|_{T\times_F U}$ through $U$. Composing either side of the identity or associativity law with $U\hookrightarrow X$ gives the corresponding law of $a$; the open inclusion is monic, so the restricted maps satisfy the laws. The inclusion is equivariant by its defining factorization. For $r=0$ the sole character is trivial; ineffective actions and every characteristic satisfy the same unit calculation.

source.place: Lemma 13.46, printed p.272, invariant eigenvector-chart calculation, here applied to a positive-degree eigen-polynomial; agent universal-test-algebra verification.

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 13.46 and Theorem 12.12 guide the weight-chart argument; missing Sumihiro quasi-projective and embedding inputs are stated separately, not attributed to Milne. Boundary removal and universal algebra calculation supplied by Q26.

lean.statement: theorem exists_sumihiro_normal_torus_affine_neighbourhood (F : Type u) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (r : ℕ) (T : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (hT : Nonempty (T ≅ MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r)) (X : CategoryTheory.Mod (Over (Spec (.of F))) T.X) [IsSeparated X.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType X.X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.X.hom] (hnormal : ∀ p : X.X.left, IsDomain (X.X.left.presheaf.stalk p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.X.left.presheaf.stalk p)) (x : X.X.left) : ∃ (U : CategoryTheory.Mod (Over (Spec (.of F))) T.X) (i : U ⟶ X), IsOpenImmersion i.hom.left ∧ IsAffine U.X.left ∧ x ∈ Set.range i.hom.left
lean.note: Uses the recorded split torus and Mathlib internal module objects. A split-torus presentation is a group-scheme isomorphism to the rank-r product. Normality is the explicit normal-domain condition on every stalk; the equivariant affine open immersion identifies its source with an invariant affine open subscheme.
